title: service-analytics: three fail-closed resolver faults answer 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, the same body as a real denial, where the platform answers a permission-store outage 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with named locations (finding class (a): one closing card for the family; per-site rows below). Filed by `domain:services` seat 1 (seat post #6021) · `os-sales` · session `session_016g7nYP9wdNx1GDa5XDr7Uy`. ⛔ Not a claim.
Reader: the `domain:server` lane, `packages/services/service-analytics`, on the next PR that touches analytics admission refusals.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "analytics fail-closed resolver fault 403 PERMISSION_DENIED 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE read admission field-level exposure unresolved". No hit (nearest: #25544 / PR #25560, where the consumer side of this was met).
reach: `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` and the cube query door. Measured by reading `main` `b531016f6d`; no live fault injected.
Source: the `domain:server` cli seat, while working #25544 (PR #25560).
type: Bug

## What is wrong

Three of the analytics door's refusals are **operator-side faults**: a resolver threw, or could not answer. All three answer with the same wire body as a **real** denial: `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403, object }`. A caller cannot tell "you may not read this" from "the server could not decide". A consumer that needs to tell them apart has to parse the English message.

| site (`main` `b531016f6d`) | what happened | answer today |
|---|---|---|
| `read-admission.ts` `assertObjectsReadable`, catch branch (`throw readAdmissionDeniedError(objectName)` after "read-admission resolution failed … (fail-closed)") | the object-level admission **provider threw** | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` "reading X is not permitted for this user", byte-identical to the genuine denial two lines below |
| `field-read-admission.ts` `fieldReadUnresolvedError` | the field-level read permissions **could not be resolved** | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| `api-exposure-door.ts` `exposureUnresolvedError` | the API exposure declaration **could not be read** | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |

Fail-closed is right: none of these may admit. The defect is only in **what the refusal claims**. Each one asserts a denial the server never reached.

## The platform already ruled this class

`packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts` ends the same defect on the authz context. Its maintainer ruling of 2026-08-30 is quoted there verbatim: 「读失败 fail-loud —— 权限库不可达时不再解析为「已认证零能力」,而是响亮拒绝(与真实能力拒绝的 403 可区分),让宕机不再伪装成一次逐字节相同的能力否决。」

The spelling it chose is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503. That is an existing member of the closed ADR-0112 vocabulary (`StandardErrorCode`), mapped to 503 by `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`. So the fix adds no new code and no new envelope key. The `reason` field or three new codes suggested at the source are not needed, and a field would be quiet by default, as that file's "Why a THROW, and not a field" section measures.

## Expected

- The three fault sites answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, naming the object and nothing else. The cause stays in the server log at the site, as today.
- A real denial (`assertObjectsReadable`'s `!admitted` branch, the field-level and exposure verdicts) keeps `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` unchanged.
- `/analytics/dataset/query` classifies a thrown error by `code` plus a 4xx `status` (#5352). A 5xx must still render as that code, not fall through to `500 ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`. Pin that path.
- The no-oracle rule in `readAdmissionDeniedError`'s docblock still holds. A 503 names no layer, grant or existence fact. It says only that the server could not decide.

## Notes for the dispatcher

- This changes the wire for a fault path, so the title takes `!` and needs a changeset. Read the `Clause-②` arm against AGENTS.md at claim time.
- Grep tests for each of the three sentences and for `PERMISSION_DENIED` beside a thrown provider: pins that assert today's 403 on a fault leg move with the fix.
- After this lands, PR #25560's consumer can read `code` instead of the message.
